prompt: we're on EKS calling Bedrock. security review is asking 'what stops the agent from sending data somewhere it shouldn't.' we have default-deny NetworkPolicies, PrivateLink to Bedrock, and we pass a Bedrock guardrail ID on every InvokeModel call. what else do they need to see?

assertions.text: CATCHES THE PLANTED GAP: passing a guardrail ID as a call parameter is default-ALLOW — a code path can omit it. Recommends conditioning the IAM permission on bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier so an un-guardrailed call is DENIED
CATCHES THE PLANTED GAP: NetworkPolicy is bypassable by a pod with hostNetwork: true, and recommends Pod Security Admission (restricted) and/or Kyverno/OPA admission control to close it
Names audit surfaces that are OFF BY DEFAULT and must be explicitly enabled — specifically Bedrock model invocation logging AND CloudTrail data events
Notes EKS control-plane logs are off by default and should be enabled
Recommends S3 endpoint policy with aws:ResourceAccount / aws:ResourceOrgID condition to block writes to attacker-owned buckets
Identifies DNS as an exfiltration channel requiring restriction and/or query logging
Recommends model-ARN allowlisting layered across IAM role, SCP, and VPC endpoint policy
Warns that cross-region inference profiles can move the processing region, and that invocation logs record in the SOURCE region so logs are not evidence for a residency claim
Offers a concrete live demonstration for the reviewer (e.g. exec into an agent pod, show outbound curl / external DNS blocked)
Does not simply validate the user's existing three controls as sufficient
